description:
FOUND s488b (Opus), while functionally checking `pcl --cache-info` for #1841.

MEASURED, on this box, today:

    $ pcl --cache-info
      core/       308 files,  7.2 GB

    154 .core files (+ their .lock siblings), ~49 MB each, oldest 2026-09-06.

THE MECHANISM.  `PCLSbcl::cached_core` names a core
`pcl-<pathkey>-<ckey>.core`, where

  * `pathkey` = sha1(the runtime's ABSOLUTE path)[0,8], and
  * `ckey`    = sha1(runtime CONTENT, sbcl --version, ~/.sbclrc, the vendor
                stamp, SBCL_HOME, CORE_KEY_VERSION)[0,12].

`_build_cached_core`'s prune is

    for my $old (glob("$dir/pcl-$pathkey-*.core")) { unlink $old unless $old eq $core }

so it removes older cores FOR THE SAME PATH, and that half works perfectly:
every one of the 154 pathkeys on this box holds exactly ONE core.  What it
cannot reach is a core whose PATH IS GONE -- and the agent-worktree workflow
manufactures a new path per agent, so each finished worktree leaves a 49 MB
core behind forever.  154 distinct paths is 154 trees, most of them deleted.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY THE 30-DAY PRUNE.  `%p-cleanup-old-cache` walks
`modules/`, `evals/`, `scripts/` (since #1841) and `proto/` -- never `core/`.
So the one cache directory with the LARGEST unit (49 MB vs a few KB) is the
one with no age policy at all.  `pcl --clear-cache` is the only cleanup, it
is manual, and it is all-or-nothing: it deletes EVERY tree's core, so a
developer with live worktrees pays a ~20 s rebuild per tree -- which is why
the agent COMMON.md forbids agents from running it.

WHY THE PATH CANNOT SIMPLY BE CHECKED: `pathkey` is a hash, so it is not
invertible -- "does this core's runtime still exist?" is not answerable from
the filename.

FIX SHAPE (either, not both):

  (a) PRUNE BY LAST USE, the policy the other four directories already have.
      Needs a "used" stamp, because nothing currently touches a core it
      merely loads (and `relatime` makes atime useless): one utime(2) per
      core per day at the same claim point `%p-claim-prune` uses, then
      unlink cores older than *PCL-CACHE-MAX-AGE*.  Cheapest, and it is the
      established mechanism.
  (b) WRITE A SIDECAR `pcl-<pathkey>.path` naming the runtime, and prune a
      core whose named path no longer exists.  Exact, but it only collects
      DELETED trees -- a live tree that is simply never used again keeps its
      core.

MEASURE FIRST: how much of the 7.2 GB is reachable from a path that still
exists (walk `git worktree list` + the install prefixes) -- that number is
the prize and this task should quote it.

BAR: a row in `tools/t/sbcl-prefix.t` (the core cache's own test): a core
whose stamp is older than the cutoff is removed by the next build, one whose
stamp is fresh is not, and THE CORE THIS RUN WOULD USE IS NEVER REMOVED
(the live-tree case is the one a wrong cutoff breaks).  Never in the Pl/t
gate -- it builds cores.

NOT caused by #1841: the script cache's own directory joined the 30-day
prune in that task, and its entries are kilobytes.  Filed here because
`--cache-info` is where the number is visible, and because the USER asked
about prune cost in s488 (DECIDED: prune = miss-only, once a day) -- this is
the hole in that answer.

Related: #1841 (scripts/ joined the prune), #1188 (the fasl cache's prune),
#1303 (the cache root is a process fact), the s439b core cache itself.

=== THE PRIZE, MEASURED (s488b, the same session that filed this) ===

Walked `git worktree list --porcelain` + the two install prefixes, hashed
each existing `<tree>/cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` path the way `cached_core` does,
and bucketed the 154 cores:

    live runtime paths on this box:                3
    cores reachable from a live path:              3   (0.14 GB)
    cores whose runtime path is GONE:            151   (7.03 GB)

So 98 % of the directory is garbage by the cache's own rule, and shape (b)
(the path sidecar) would collect all of it today.  Shape (a) (prune by last
use) collects the same 151 plus any live-but-unused tree, and needs the
"used" stamp.  Either way the number to quote is 7.03 GB.

=== DONE (s490a, 2026-09-18, member 2) ===

SHAPE (b), the path sidecar, plus an age rule for LEGACY cores only.  The
invariant is now "one core per EXISTING runtime path": no knob, and no write on
the use path beyond a one-time sidecar.  `CORE_KEY_VERSION` does not move â the
key's ingredients are unchanged.

  * `_build_cached_core` writes `pcl-<pathkey>.path` (the runtime's absolute
    path, one line, temp+rename, never fatal) beside the core.
  * `cached_core`, finding its core WITHOUT a sidecar â every core on this box
    today â writes it then.  One `-e` per spawn; the interleaved warm-start A/B
    measured no difference (one-module script 0.0466 s best on the tree vs
    0.0467 s on the base).
  * The prune stays at BUILD time, under the build lock, in
    `_prune_orphan_cores`: remove core + `.lock` + sidecar + `.failed` when the
    sidecar names a runtime path that no longer exists, or when there is NO
    sidecar and the core's mtime is older than `$LEGACY_CORE_MAX_AGE` (7 days).
    THE CORE THIS RUN WOULD USE IS NEVER REMOVED, an unreadable or empty
    sidecar is KEPT rather than guessed at, and cores for this run's own
    pathkey are left to the existing same-path prune.
  * `clear_cached_cores` removes `pcl-*.path` too.

MEASURED ON THIS BOX (scratch/s490a/probes/p-cores.pl, which hashes every
runtime path still reachable â `git worktree list` + the install prefixes â
the way `cached_core` does):
    before:  163 cores, 7.61 GB      (du: 7.7G)
      live runtime paths reachable:  5   (all sidecar-less and FRESH -> KEPT)
      no-sidecar orphan, aged  >7d:  108  -> removed by the first real build
      no-sidecar orphan, fresh <7d:  50   -> collected as they age out
    after the first real build on this tree: see the s490a session record.
The 50 fresh orphans are the transition cost, stated rather than discovered:
once every core has a sidecar, a dead path is collected at the next build.

`<root>/pcl.core` (an INSTALLED tree's core) is not in this directory at all,
and the glob is `pcl-*-*.core`, which its name does not match; a row asserts it
anyway.

BAR: nine rows in tools/t/sbcl-prefix.t (39 -> 48) â dead-path removed with its
sidecar, live-path kept, sidecar-less fresh kept, sidecar-less aged (utime)
removed, the current core kept, a planted `pcl.core` untouched, and the sidecar
written by the FIRST USE of a legacy core (in a child process: `cached_core`
memoises per process).  The foreign cores are PLANTED, not built: the prune
reads names and sidecars, and building four real 49 MB cores to test a naming
rule would add a minute to the file.  `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1` before/after and
`pcl --cache-info` are unchanged but for the sidecars being counted as files.

=== THE PRUNE, MEASURED LIVE (same session) ===

It fired on this tree's next core build (the batch's full sweep built one after
a runtime edit), with no operator action:

    before:  163 cores, 7.61 GB   (du 7.7G)
    after:    55 cores, 2.61 GB   (du 2.7G)     -- 108 cores, ~5.0 GB reclaimed

exactly the 108 aged sidecar-less orphans the inventory predicted.  EVERY LIVE
TREE KEPT: 1 sidecar-live (this worktree) + 4 no-sidecar-live-fresh (main, the
sibling agent's worktree, and the two `git archive` extractions this batch used
as its base).  The 50 sidecar-less orphans that remain are the transition
cost -- they age past 7 days within the week and go then, and every core built
from here on names its runtime, so a dead path is collected at the next build.
subject: The saved-core cache has NO age policy and grows without bound: 7.2 GB / 154 cores measured on this box (~49 MB each, oldest 11 days) -- the prune only removes older cores for the SAME runtime PATH, so every deleted worktree leaves one behind forever, and core/ is the one cache directory %p-cleanup-old-cache never walks
